checks: For h<1/k both thresholds are positive because β<k/3, and their threshold-to-radius ratios have the stated positive derivative numerators and tend to infinity at the leg endpoint. Both tails therefore vanish strictly before radius zero.

For 1/2<a<2/3 the second derivative of the lower branch is 2(k²−β²/(ac))>0, since ac≥2/9 and β²<k²/9. The upper proper branch is an affine square and its first derivative vanishes when the cap empties. At s=cr the two formulas and each first partial derivative match.

At a=1/2 the endpoint tail is the positive part of r²−4s² for positive s. Its derivative jumps upward to zero at the terminal knot because k>2β. An initially empty branch is identically zero. Convex trapezoids give J≥I+O/2 and the first pair gives J≥O; their convex combination yields the first inequality including k=1.

The two-squared-hinge formula integrates to p³/(3ℓ) per active hinge, with positive steps including ck−β. The right thresholds change branches exactly at β=L and β=U; the removed squared hinge and its integral vanish at each transition, so shared boundaries are valid.

The three substitutions cover the original β interval, and w=(k−3β)/(1−3β)∈(0,1]. Every denominator is strictly positive on the required range with 1/2<a<2/3, β<k/3. For region 2, 1−3β=3L(1−v) and 3c−1=3L, so ck−β contains the factor L after substitution.

Independent exact rational expansion reconstructed the three mapped numerator polynomials and the polynomial denominators. A tensor binomial generating-polynomial transformation produced 819, 528, 528, 528 and 200 coefficients, matching all archived entries and the minima 0, 0, 0, 0 and 21/128. The three region-1 boxes cover the full square and nonnegative Bernstein basis functions prove positivity on each mapped cube.

With k,β fixed, dominated convergence on [0,1/k] gives the a↓1/2 limit of I and the pointwise convergence at h=0 gives that of O. The limiting nonzero normal has an area-null boundary, and the zero-radius values are zero. No denominator division is needed at the extra polynomial boundary.
The original Lemmas 1–3 contain the same scalar bound, domain, multipliers and exact coefficient certificate. The larger arbitrary-chain reduction is not needed for this claim.

dependencies.hypotheses: The accepted proof gives exactly the two proper-tail quadratics of the planar scaled standard triangle at 1/2<a<2/3, and the equal-height formula at a=1/2. The present proof verifies their convexity and integrated coefficient certificate separately.

overlap.comparison: The accepted planar low-normal theorem supplies a cap surplus for the actual chain, using an affine-leg envelope and an own-cap bonus. It does not assert the combined real integral and initial pair inequality proved here.

The accepted full-leg envelope bound uses the diagonal envelope over the sampled leg. The present certificate uses the exact positive-normal triangle tails integrated over the real leg and has a different numerical right side.
